Reading is optional but each item is here for a reason. Start with the two marked **start
here** if you read nothing else.

## Papers

**Watson JD, Crick FHC (1953).** *Molecular structure of nucleic acids: a structure for
deoxyribose nucleic acid.* Nature 171:737–738.
[doi:10.1038/171737a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/171737a0)

> One page. Worth reading once for how much of what we exploit was visible immediately:
> antiparallel strands, the complementarity that every hybridisation step depends on.

**Lehman IR (1974).** *DNA ligase: structure, mechanism, and function.* Science
186:790–797. [doi:10.1126/science.186.4166.790](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.186.4166.790)
— **start here**

> Why a ligase needs a 5'-phosphate and a free 3'-OH, and what the enzyme is actually doing
> with ATP. Every adapter ligation in the course rests on this.

**Clark JM (1988).** *Novel non-templated nucleotide addition reactions catalyzed by
procaryotic and eucaryotic DNA polymerases.* Nucleic Acids Research 16:9677–9686.
[doi:10.1093/nar/16.20.9677](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/16.20.9677)

> The original description of non-templated 3' A addition. This accident of polymerase
> behaviour became the A-tailing step in nearly every DNA library prep.

**SantaLucia J (1998).** *A unified view of polymer, dumbbell, and oligonucleotide DNA
nearest-neighbor thermodynamics.* PNAS 95:1460–1465.
[doi:10.1073/pnas.95.4.1460](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.95.4.1460)

> Where predicted Tm values come from. Skim the model and the tables; you do not need the
> derivations, but you should know that Tm is a property of a duplex in a buffer, not of an
> oligo on its own.

**Kivioja T, et al. (2011).** *Counting absolute numbers of molecules using unique molecular
identifiers.* Nature Methods 9:72–74.
[doi:10.1038/nmeth.1778](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.1778)

> The idea that a degenerate stretch of `N` bases makes each starting molecule individually
> countable. Returned to in depth later in the course.

**Eckstein F (2014).** *Phosphorothioates, essential components of therapeutic
oligonucleotides.* Nucleic Acid Therapeutics 24:374–387.
[doi:10.1089/nat.2014.0506](https://doi.org/10.1089/nat.2014.0506)

> Written for therapeutics, but it is the clearest account of what a phosphorothioate linkage
> does and why nucleases cannot cut it — the reason it appears in exonuclease-resistant
> primers and adapters.

**Head SR, et al. (2014).** *Library construction for next-generation sequencing: overviews
and challenges.* BioTechniques 56:61–77.
[doi:10.2144/000114133](https://doi.org/10.2144/000114133) — **start here**

> A survey of what goes wrong in library prep: adapter dimers, bias, low input. Read it now
> for orientation, and again after the building-block modules.

## Reference material to keep open

- **[NGS 101](https://henriksson-lab.github.io/NGS_101/)** — every protocol in the collection
  drawn base by base, with the end state at each step. The *Annotate sequence* tab identifies
  adapter and primer parts in a sequence you paste; *Anneal primers* shows how two oligos pair.
- **[NEB selection charts](https://www.neb.com/en/tools-and-resources/selection-charts)** —
  polymerases, ligases, nucleases side by side. The polymerase chart's columns (fidelity,
  3'→5' exonuclease, 5'→3' exonuclease, strand displacement, resulting 3' ends, dU tolerance)
  are the properties this course asks you to reason with. You will use it in the exercises.
- **[IDT OligoAnalyzer](https://eu.idtdna.com/pages/tools/oligoanalyzer)** — Tm, hairpins and
  self-dimers for a sequence you type in. Free, requires an account.
- Any supplier's **oligo modification list** — worth browsing once to see what can be put on
  an oligo end.

## Related protocols in the collection

Once you have the end-state habit, look at how these differ in their first few steps:

- [TruSeq DNA PCR-Free](https://henriksson-lab.github.io/NGS_101/) — shear, end repair,
  A-tail, ligate: the canonical sequence of end transformations
- [NEBNext Ultra II DNA with USER adaptor](https://henriksson-lab.github.io/NGS_101/) — a
  hairpin adapter containing dU, opened later by USER
- [Nextera XT](https://henriksson-lab.github.io/NGS_101/) — no end repair at all, because
  tagmentation creates the ends and attaches the handle in one step

Exact links for every protocol are in `planning/protocol_links.tsv` in the course repository.
